basis: NMJ dysfunction defines CMS; muscle-fiber atrophy and fixed joint abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Ptosis and ophthalmoplegia reflect neuromuscular weakness, not intrinsic eye damage.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis (80-99%) and ophthalmoplegia (30-79%) arise from NMJ dysfunction; they do not establish direct damage to ocular tissues.

basis: Neuroendocrine tumour originating in extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglia; catecholamine secretion defines endocrine involvement. No additional common organ damage established.

decisions.neurologic: primary: tumour originates in sympathetic paraganglia, components of the peripheral autonomic nervous system.

basis: Hereditary motor neuronopathy; structural muscle wasting in 7/8 and biopsy atrophy in 2/3; left ventricular hypertrophy in 2/6 (~33%). Cardiac estimate has a small denominator.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: actual muscle loss, not weakness alone, is documented by distal amyotrophy in 7/8 and muscle-fiber atrophy in 2/3.

basis: Inborn O-glycosylation disorder with defining muscular dystrophy and brain malformations. Retinal dysplasia occurs in 20/20; ocular disease is placed in involved because of the primary cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: defining structural eye disease, including retinal dysplasia in 20/20; the three-primary cap places ocular involvement here.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is an inborn disorder of protein O-glycosylation, so the metabolic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Deafness and anhidrotic ectodermal dysplasia define hearing, sweat-gland/hair and characteristic dental-development abnormalities; subtype-specific phenotype detail is sparse.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: characteristic abnormal dentition is a defining component of anhidrotic ectodermal dysplasia; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Inherited insulin excess causes hypoglycemia; persistent neurodevelopmental injury occurs in roughly 30-50% of congenital cases, which dominate this umbrella. Frequency varies by severity.

decisions.neurologic: involved: recurrent neuroglycopenia directly injures the brain; lasting neurodevelopmental impairment affects approximately 30-50% of congenital cases.

basis: DOK7-related postsynaptic NMJ disease; structural muscle involvement includes tongue atrophy in 4/10 (40%). Ptosis and reduced vital capacity reflect neuromuscular weakness.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: tongue atrophy in 4/10 (40%) establishes common structural muscle loss; the defining lesion is at the NMJ rather than a primary dystrophy.

basis: Immunodeficiency and microcephaly define NBS. HPO reports anal malformations at 80-99%, an atypical estimate retained here; autoimmune cytopenias and lymphomas are separate complications.

decisions.haematologic: none: autoimmune cytopenias and lymphomas are separately diagnosed complications; lymphopenia belongs to the defining immunodeficiency.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: supplied HPO assigns anal atresia/stenosis 80-99%; these are direct structural defects, although this frequency is clinically atypical.

basis: Absent respiratory cilia cause chronic airway disease. Chronic otitis is described as typical lifelong involvement, supporting >=30% with persistent ear inflammation; exact frequency is unavailable.

decisions.otologic: involved: typical lifelong chronic otitis supports common (approximately >=30%) persistent ear inflammation associated with ciliary dysfunction, rather than transient symptoms.

basis: Heterotaxy with congenital cardiac malformations; asplenia in 2/3 and hydronephrosis in 2/2 support splenic and renal involvement. Small denominators limit certainty; situs alone is not damage.

decisions.renal: involved: hydronephrosis is structural urinary-tract pathology, reported in 2/2 assessed patients; the supplied frequency supports inclusion with limited certainty.
